prompts.title: Politely decline a request by email
prompts.description: Write a short, warm email that says no without burning the relationship, and offers an alternative.
prompts.exampleOutput:
Subject: Re: Speaking at your offsite

Hi Sam, thank you for thinking of me for the offsite. I can't take this one on because my calendar is full through March. I'd be glad to recommend a colleague, or to join a call later in the spring. Thanks again for the invitation.

Best,
Alex

prompts.title: Write a search result meta description
prompts.description: Produce three meta description options under 155 characters that match the page's search intent.

variables.label: Benefit
variables.default: a clear checklist they can use today

prompts.exampleOutput:
1. Learn how to compare standing desks with this simple checklist covering height range, stability and warranty.
2. Standing desk buying guide: the five specs that matter, plus a printable checklist.
3. Not sure which standing desk to buy? Use this checklist to compare height, stability and price.

prompts.title: Explain this error and suggest a fix
prompts.description: Paste a stack trace and get the likely cause, a minimal fix and how to confirm it worked.
prompts.body:
You are a senior {{language:select(TypeScript, Python, Go, Java)|TypeScript}} developer. Explain the error below.

Error and stack trace:
{{error:long}}

Respond with: 1) the most likely root cause in two sentences, 2) a minimal code fix, 3) one way to verify the fix, 4) one other possible cause if the first fix does not work.
prompts.exampleOutput:
1. Root cause: `user` is undefined because the fetch has not resolved when render runs.
2. Fix: guard with `if (!user) return null;` before reading `user.name`.
3. Verify: reload the page; the TypeError should no longer appear.
4. Otherwise: the API may return null for new accounts.

prompts.title: Explain a metric change in plain language
prompts.description: Turn a metric movement into a short explanation with likely causes and the checks to run first.

variables.label: Context
variables.default: No known releases or campaigns this week.

prompts.exampleOutput: Summary: Weekly signups fell 12%, mostly on mobile. Likely causes: 1) a slower signup page, 2) a seasonal dip, 3) lower paid traffic. First checks: page speed, last year's same week, ad spend.

prompts.title: Draft a one-page decision memo
prompts.description: Structure a decision into context, options, a recommendation and the risks that would change it.

variables.label: Constraints
variables.default: Budget is fixed; decide by Friday.

prompts.exampleOutput:
Context: We must choose a support tool by Friday.
Options: A (cheap, basic), B (mid, integrations).
Recommendation: B.
Risks: setup time.
What would change my mind: a failed pilot.

prompts.title: Explain a concept at three levels
prompts.description: Get a concept explained for a child, a student and an expert, with one analogy and one common mistake.
prompts.body: Explain {{topic}} at three levels: a ten-year-old, a first-year student and a practitioner. Add one analogy and one common misconception for each level. Keep each level under 80 words.
prompts.exampleOutput:
Ten-year-old: Compound interest is when your savings earn money, and then that money earns money too.
Student: Interest is added to the balance each period, so growth is exponential.
Practitioner: Frequency of compounding changes the effective annual rate.

prompts.title: Plan my week from a messy list
prompts.description: Turn a brain dump into a realistic weekly plan with priorities and protected focus time.
prompts.exampleOutput:
Priorities: 1) finish budget draft, 2) client call prep, 3) hire shortlist.
Mon: budget draft (3h), small tasks (1h), buffer.
Tue: call prep (2h), shortlist (2h), buffer.

prompts.title: Tighten an interview answer
prompts.description: Improve a rambling interview answer into a clear story with a result and a lesson.
prompts.exampleOutput: Situation: Our onboarding emails had a low open rate. Action: I rewrote subject lines and tested three versions. Result: opens rose from 22% to 31%. Follow-ups: How did you pick the winner? What would you test next?

prompts.title: Reply to an upset customer
prompts.description: Draft a calm reply that acknowledges the problem, owns the next step and sets a clear time.

variables.label: What we can offer
variables.default: a refund or a free replacement

prompts.exampleOutput: Hi Dana, I'm sorry the order arrived damaged. I've sent a replacement today and you'll get tracking by 5 pm. If you would prefer a refund instead, just reply and I'll process it right away.

prompts.title: Create a vivid character sketch
prompts.description: Build a character with a want, a flaw, a secret and a few concrete habits you can use in a scene.
prompts.exampleOutput: Name: Ines Calder, harbor clerk. Wants: to be believed. Flaw: counts everything. Secret: she forged a ledger. Habits: hums off-key, ties knots in receipts. Voice: "I've counted twice, and the boat is still missing."

prompts.title: Plan a week of simple dinners
prompts.description: Get five dinners, one shopping list and a prep tip around your time and diet.
prompts.body:
Plan five weeknight dinners for {{people:number|2}} people.

Dietary needs: {{diet:text|no restrictions}}
Time per meal: {{minutes:number|30}} minutes

Give a one-line description for each dinner, one combined shopping list grouped by aisle, and one prep tip for Sunday.
prompts.exampleOutput:
Mon: lemon chicken with rice. Tue: veggie chili. Wed: pasta with spinach. Thu: tacos. Fri: sheet-pan salmon.
Shopping: produce (spinach, lemons), protein, pantry (rice, pasta).

prompts.title: Product photo prompt for an image model
prompts.description: A structured text-to-image prompt for a clean product shot with lighting, lens and background specified.
prompts.exampleOutput: A ceramic coffee mug on a pale oak table, soft window light from the left, 85mm lens, shallow depth of field, neutral grey backdrop, 4:5. Negative: text, watermark, blurry edges.
